transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

That musty smell is usually caused by moisture trapped in the clothes or the machine itself. The most common reasons are that the load was too big for the drying function (washer-dryers can only dry about half their wash capacity), the spin cycle didn't remove enough water first, or fluff has blocked the filter/condenser so damp air isn't being vented properly. Please try these two checks:
1. Check the pump filter and condenser: Unplug the machine, place towels under the bottom front panel, unscrew the filter slowly to catch any water, and clean out any fluff or debris. If your model has a separate condenser unit (usually behind a grille near the filter), remove it and rinse it under cold water until clear.
2. Run a hot empty cycle: With no clothes inside, run a cotton cycle at 60°C or higher with a cup of white vinegar or a washing machine cleaner tablet to kill any mould spores in the drum and seals. Once you've done that, let me know if the smell persists on your next wash.

ok will try. the filter is smelly sludge and fluff when i looked, and the door seal has black spots and grey sludge in the bottom fold. is that the problem? the 60 degree wash with vinegar is fine to do?

Yes, that is exactly the problem. The black spots and grey sludge in the door seal are mould colonies feeding on the dampness trapped there, which is what smells so musty. Your filter was also full of fluff, which restricts airflow during drying and leaves clothes damp. The 60°C wash with vinegar is fine to do—it will help kill some spores—but it won't remove the physical mould in the seal folds. You need to manually clean the rubber door seal: pull back the folds gently and wipe them thoroughly with a cloth soaked in hot water and washing-up liquid (or a mild bleach solution if you prefer, but rinse well). After cleaning, always leave the door and detergent drawer slightly ajar when not in use to let air circulate. If the smell persists after this deep clean and your next wash/dry cycle, it may indicate mould deeper in the drum or internal pipes, but start with the seal.

candidates: Residual moisture from poor spin or overloading (high)
Blocked lint filter or condenser causing damp air recirculation (medium)
Detergent residue or door seal mould (hygiene issue) (medium)
